description:
## Purpose
Establish the pre-refactor compatibility baseline before changing execution paths. Reconcile this plan with current HEAD and preserve unrelated working-tree changes.

## Scope
Inspect and characterize lib/jido_ai.ex facades, model_aliases.ex, action/directive consumers, reasoning/react/{config,strategy,runner,token}.ex, output.ex and reasoning/chain_of_thought/worker/strategy.ex. Capture exact generation response passthrough, native stream_text/2 return, object generation, aliases and rich model inputs, keyword/string-keyed option maps, HTTP/provider forwarding, single/batch embeddings, existing errors/signals, WebSocket reuse and response continuation. Include current scripted Jido.AI.Test behavior.
Create independent pre-change checkpoint fixtures (not tokens generated only by new code). Audit all direct/aliased/dynamic ReqLLM calls and backend-relevant schema/option allowlists, including child workers and repair/tool followups. Record drift from the original research in this issue before changing contracts.

## Acceptance criteria
- Focused baseline tests cover default return shapes and options without live provider calls.
- Checkpoint fixtures exercise existing token/fingerprint/response-ID behavior.
- Complete migration inventory distinguishes allowed shared data helpers from executable provider integration.
- Existing unknown-capability/string-model behavior is recorded so eager validation cannot accidentally break it.

## Suggested commit
 test(backend): characterize existing llm integration contracts

comments.text:
Characterization complete on 17c10b55 (req_llm 1.24.0, llm_db 2026.9.4). Added six focused offline baseline tests in test/jido_ai/backend_compatibility_test.exs: literal pre-backend compressed rt2 checkpoint and fingerprint, compatible restore/incompatible model rejection, generation/object ReqLLM.Response identity and options, native ReqLLM.StreamResponse without eager consumption, unknown string model acceptance/unknown alias rejection, and ordered embedding action result. mix test focused: 6 tests, 0 failures; mix format --check-formatted focused: OK.

Migration inventory (all executable call sites): lib/jido_ai.ex (3 facades); lib/jido_ai/actions/{llm/chat,llm/complete,llm/embed,llm/generate_object,planning/decompose,planning/plan,planning/prioritize,reasoning/analyze,reasoning/explain,reasoning/infer,tool_calling/call_with_tools}.ex; lib/jido_ai/directive/{llm_generate,llm_stream,llm_embed}.ex; lib/jido_ai/output.ex repair; lib/jido_ai/reasoning/chain_of_thought/worker/strategy.ex; lib/jido_ai/reasoning/react/runner.ex; lib/jido_ai/tool_adapter.ex doctext only. Model/option provider calls: lib/jido_ai/model_aliases.ex, lib/jido_ai.ex, reasoning/react/{config,strategy,runner}.ex. ReAct runner also calls StreamResponse.process_stream/usage, websocket provider modules, Streaming.WebSocketSession.close; CoT worker directly consumes .stream, Response.Stream.summarize and StreamResponse.usage. Streaming directive consumes StreamResponse.process_stream. Tool-calling action performs post-tool follow-up. Output repair independently calls generate_object. Explicit option forwarding also occurs in agent.ex, request.ex, plugins, action run_strategy allowlists, directive helpers, strategy builders and CLI adapters.

Allowed shared pure-data helpers outside ReqLLM adapter (to review function by function): ReqLLM.Message/Context/Tool/ToolCall/ContentPart construction; ReqLLM.Response struct/classify/usage/unwrap_object; ReqLLM.StreamChunk and Response.Stream summary; ReqLLM.Schema validation/conversion. Do NOT blanket-allow ReqLLM.Response namespace: decode_response/decode_object can invoke provider/model logic.

Drift versus original research: current HEAD req_llm is ~>1.14 in mix.exs but lock resolved 1.24.0, not older versions; local deps initially stale llm_db 2026.7.5 despite lock 2026.9.4. Refetched only llm_db checkout via mix deps.clean llm_db + mix deps.get. No tracked dependency changes. Alias resolve_model/1 lets unknown binary specs pass unchanged; direct non-string rich alias forms are validated by ReqLLM.model. Existing Token uses signed rt2 payload and Config.fingerprint has no backend identity. Existing tests also use fake map responses; subsequent dispatcher migration must preserve those test seams or adjust carefully. User AGENTS.md and untracked .serena/ are pre-existing and untouched.

title: Characterize existing LLM integration and compatibility contracts
